items.one_liner: Armory Castle exploited VMware vCenter CVE-2026-123890 and BeyondTrust zero-days to deploy BONESAW and compromise enterprise infrastructure.
items.summary: The suspected China-nexus cyber espionage group Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited a critical unauthenticated authentication bypass zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS score: 9.8) in the VMware Directory Service of VMware vCenter Server in early September 2026. The attackers used a Golang-based remote exploitation utility called BONESAW to exfiltrate the LMDB database, hijack the SAML Security Token Service, and create an SSO administrator account. This campaign also leveraged a zero-day in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS score: 9.3) to gain initial access, deploy the BARECLAW proxy tunneler, and move laterally to internal appliances using tools like nmap and JSP web shells. Broadcom released patches for vCenter and Cloud Foundation on November 19, 2026.

CVE-2026-102764: CVSS 9.3, BeyondTrust Remote Support vulnerability
Malware families: BONESAW, BARECLAW, SLIMSAVAGE, CAGEMATCH, SAWSNAKE
items.bottom_line: Administrators must immediately patch VMware vCenter Server against CVE-2026-123890 to prevent unauthenticated attacker session creation and data exfiltration.

items.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
items.one_liner: ARISE provides a memory architecture for enterprise LLM agents that learns from failures via iterative self-evaluation without altering model weights.
items.summary: Researchers propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture enabling enterprise LLM agents to evolve from their own failures without updating underlying model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE attributes failures using the model itself or a teacher model, stores corrections as retrievable micro memories, consolidates them into macro rules, and updates rules only when held-out accuracy increases. Across enterprise workflow domains, ARISE-Teacher using Claude Opus 4.6 yields significant accuracy gains over baselines while using fewer model calls and output tokens.

items.bottom_line: Self-evolving agent memory frameworks can improve enterprise LLM task accuracy and reduce execution costs without weight updates.

items.title: Attackers bypass GitHub SHA pinning with malicious fork commits
items.one_liner: Attackers are exploiting GitHub fork networks to bypass SHA pinning in CI/CD pipelines, forcing the adoption of workflow lockfiles.
items.summary: Attackers have bypassed GitHub Actions SHA pinning by planting malicious commits inside fork networks and labeling them as security fixes, exploiting a gap between code immutability and provenance. Incidents in March and May 2026 targeted popular tools like Trivy and actions-cool/issues-helper, using fork-derived commits to execute arbitrary code within CI pipelines holding cloud credentials. While SHA pinning freezes code bytes, it does not verify who authored the commit or whether it belongs to the upstream repository branch. GitHub attempted to mitigate this threat by introducing workflow lockfiles, which require locked commits to reside on upstream branch networks, though runtime dependency builds and authorship visibility remain security challenges.
key_facts: Lockfile availability: General availability on October 28, 2026
items.bottom_line: SHA pinning alone cannot prevent supply-chain compromises if an attacker can inject malicious commits into a project's wider fork network.

items.title: Bridge Agent Memory Beats SOTA on Recall Benchmarks
items.one_liner: The Bridge agent memory framework matches SOTA recall benchmarks on a lean token budget but highlights gaps in applied production tasks.
items.summary: Researchers from the University of Chicago and UC Berkeley introduced 'Bridge,' a minimalist memory stack for AI agents that matches published state-of-the-art recall benchmark scores while consuming only 5,000 to 7,000 reader tokens per query. Bridge combines session ingestion blocks with an extractor LLM, dual-channel BM25 and cosine retrieval fused via reciprocal rank fusion, and chronological note re-sorting.
